key_insight: A learned latent-dynamics module captures history-dependent deformations (e.g., loose clothing, inertia, contacts) and integrates with pose-driven neural rendering to produce temporally coherent full-body avatar animation from raw multi-view capture without requiring dedicated garment templates.
problem_solved: Pose-only controllers cannot explain dynamic elements: the same pose can correspond to many different cloth/body states because of history, inertia, and contact; this paper addresses how to model those ambiguous, time-dependent deformations without explicit garment templates or hand-crafted simulation.
method: Encode per-frame appearance/deformation into a compact latent state learned from multi-view capture.
Predict latent-state evolution with a temporal dynamics network conditioned on pose history, then decode into neural-rendered geometry/appearance for each frame.
Train end-to-end on raw multi-view data, avoiding dedicated garment templates or explicit physical simulation while capturing realistic, history-dependent motion.
impact: Enables more realistic, temporally coherent avatar animations (especially for loose clothing and other dynamic elements) while simplifying capture-to-avatar pipelines. Useful for VR/AR, telepresence, game characters, and any application needing plausible motion without costly simulation or manual garment modeling.
visual_elements: Before/after sequence: same input pose rendered with and without latent dynamics to show different cloth states over time.
Pipeline diagram: multi-view capture → latent encoder → dynamics module (conditioned on pose history) → decoder/neural renderer.
Latent-space visualization: trajectories of latent states for different motion snippets to illustrate history dependence.
Side-by-side comparisons: ground truth multi-view frames vs. rendered outputs highlighting cloth wrinkles and temporal coherence.
paper_title: Latent Dynamics for Full Body Avatar Animation
paper_authors: Shichong Peng, Chengxiang Yin, Fei Jiang, Zhongshi Jiang, Lingchen Yang
